CFML Language Reference: Functions

ParseDateTime

Reads a string containing a date, a time or both and returns a real date/time value.

Category

Date and time functions

Syntax

ParseDateTime(date_string [, pop_conversion_method ])

Parameters

date_string
A string such as "10/22/1999", "Oct 22, 1999 9:42 PM", "22-Oct-99", "1999-10-22 21:42:00" or an ODBC escape such as {ts '1999-10-22 21:42:00'}.
pop_conversion_method
Optional. "POP" or "STANDARD", for dates read from Internet mail headers. Accepted for compatibility; KoldFusion ignores it.

Returns

A date/time value.

Usage

Numeric dates are read in US order, month/day/year (or year-month-day when the year comes first). Month names can be full or three letters, and weekday names are skipped. Times may use AM/PM or the 24-hour clock; a time on its own gets the zero date, December 30, 1899.

Two-digit years are converted with a sliding window: 00 to 29 become 2000 to 2029, and 30 to 99 become 1930 to 1999. So "1/1/29" is in 2029 and "1/1/30" is in 1930. This applies everywhere KoldFusion converts a string to a date, not just here. We recommend four-digit years anyway; the year 2030 will come sooner than you think.

A string that is not a valid date throws a parameter validation error; test it first with IsDate.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFOUTPUT>
<TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
<TR><TH>String</TH><TH>ParseDateTime</TH></TR>
<CFLOOP INDEX="S" LIST="10/22/1999|Oct 22 1999 9:42 PM|Friday 22-Oct-99|1999-10-22 21:42:00|1/1/00|1/1/29|1/1/30|14:30" DELIMITERS="|">
<TR><TD>#S#</TD><TD>#ParseDateTime(S)#</TD></TR>
</CFLOOP>
</TABLE>
</CFOUTPUT>
